dedupe_keys.name: high resolution 10 km 10 km anthropogenic methane emissions in china in 2020

description: Researchers at Hainan University, Tsinghua University and partner institutions publish a bottom-up estimate of anthropogenic methane emissions in China for 2020. The January 2023 Zenodo release provides one archive under CC BY 4.0, free to download. Its description covers 45 subsectors and approximately 130,000 point sources, grouped into fossil-fuel and food systems. Annual emissions are allocated to a 0.1-by-0.1-degree grid, approximately ten kilometres, using source coordinates where available and provincial surrogate indicators elsewhere. These estimates can supply spatial emissions inputs or comparison targets for coupled infrastructure and atmospheric simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this inventory. The grid is an allocation of annual estimates, not continuous direct measurement or a complete public point-source register. Internal format, sector-level file availability, emission units and uncertainty ranges remain unverified. Proxy allocation and variable cell area should be considered before local interpretation.
